title: Qunnect and Monarch Quantum Partner for Commercializing and Deploying Quantum Networking Technologies Using Advanced Manufacturing - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Qunnect and Monarch Quantum have partnered to shrink Qunnect's Carina entanglement distribution platform from a 36U rack to a 2U or 3U form factor using Monarch's robotic, machine-vision co-packaged optics assembly — with the final size hinging on whether non-cryogenic photon detectors can be integrated into the optical packages. Monarch is scaling to a 60,000 sq ft San Diego facility by year end with an 8,000 sq ft clean room holding 20-25 robotic assembly stations, targeting SWaP-constrained buyers in satellites, defense, telecom, edge and IoT.

insights.claim: Qunnect's Carina turnkey entanglement distribution platform currently occupies a 36U rack panel containing photon generators, polarization compensators and photon detectors, and the partnership targets shrinking that to a 2U or 3U form factor.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: A 12-18x rack-space reduction is the gating step that turns quantum networking gear from a lab installation into a deployable telecom line card.
insights.quote: the goal will be to reduce this to a 2U or 3U form factor, depending upon whether they can integrate non-cryogenic photon detectors into the optical packages
insights.locator: For Qunnect, this will enable to them to reduce the cost and size

insights.claim: Whether Carina lands at 2U or 3U depends specifically on integrating non-cryogenic photon detectors into the optical packages — making room-temperature single-photon detection the explicit technical dependency in the roadmap.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Cryogenic detectors are the hidden cost and size driver in quantum networking; suppliers of non-cryogenic single-photon detectors sit on the critical path for the whole deployment thesis.
insights.quote: depending upon whether they can integrate non-cryogenic photon detectors into the optical packages
insights.locator: For Qunnect, this will enable to them to reduce the cost and size

insights.claim: The partnership is expected to cut both cost and size of Qunnect's systems by many times, not incrementally — framing manufacturing engineering, rather than physics, as the current bottleneck in quantum networking.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: When a quantum company's next unlock is packaging rather than physics, the investable layer shifts to photonic packaging and assembly specialists.
insights.quote: For Qunnect, this will enable to them to reduce the cost and size of their systems by many times.
insights.locator: For Qunnect, this will enable to them

themes.theme: Robotic assembly as the photon-loss lever

insights.claim: In photonic systems the dominant engineering objective is minimizing photon loss, and Monarch's co-packaged optics with precise, repeatable component alignment is positioned as the mechanism for delivering that improvement.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Alignment precision translates directly into link budget and reach for entanglement distribution — the physical constraint that determines how far apart quantum network nodes can sit.
insights.quote: In a photonic system it is important to reduce photon losses in the system as much as possible.
insights.locator: Monarch has expertise in robotic, machine-vision guided manufacturing

insights.claim: Monarch achieves its alignment precision through robotic, machine-vision guided assembly that the article states produces much better results than manual assembly — the same automation shift that industrialized classical optics.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Quantum hardware is following the classical photonics playbook: manual-to-robotic assembly is where unit cost curves break, and it is the sign a category is leaving the lab.
insights.quote: They accomplish this using robotic assembly which provides much better results than manual assembly.
insights.locator: Monarch has expertise in robotic, machine-vision guided manufacturing

themes.theme: Physical capacity buildout in San Diego

insights.claim: Monarch Quantum is transitioning to a 60,000 square foot San Diego facility by the end of 2026, an unusually large footprint for a quantum photonics manufacturer.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Floor space is a hard, verifiable signal of expected production volume — 60,000 sq ft implies orders well beyond current quantum networking demand.
insights.quote: Monarch will be transitioning to a 60,000 square foot facility in San Diego by the end of the year.
insights.locator: Monarch has expertise in robotic, machine-vision guided manufacturing

insights.claim: An 8,000 square foot clean room expansion scheduled for operation in September will contain 20 to 25 robotic assembly stations, giving a concrete near-term measure of the partnership's production capacity.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: 20-25 stations coming online in September is the nearest checkable milestone; slippage there delays every downstream Qunnect miniaturization claim.
insights.quote: 8,000 square foot clean room expansion schedule for operation in September will contain 20 to 25 robotic assembly stations
insights.locator: They will also have a 8,000 square foot clean room

themes.theme: Target markets and the Orian product line

insights.claim: The next-generation hardware is aimed at size, weight, power and operational constrained deployments — satellites, defense platforms, remote infrastructure, edge computing, telecommunications and IoT — a market list far broader than research quantum networks.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: SWaP-constrained entanglement hardware opens defense and space procurement channels, where budgets are far less sensitive to the absence of a near-term quantum computing payoff.
insights.quote: designed for deployment in environments with strict size, weight, power, and operational constraints—including satellites, defense platforms, remote infrastructure, edge computing, telecommunications, and IoT environments
insights.locator: The next-generation hardware is designed for deployment

insights.claim: Qunnect plans a use-case-packaged version of Carina codenamed Orian, moving from selling a general-purpose entanglement platform to selling specific applications.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Productizing by use case is how infrastructure vendors escape science-project procurement cycles; watch whether Orian ships with fixed pricing.
insights.quote: Future products for Qunnect would include a version of Carina, codenamed Orian, packaged with specific use cases.
insights.locator: The next-generation hardware is designed for deployment

insights.claim: The named Orian use cases are Quantum Position Verification to certify server or client locations and Quantum Alarm to detect fiber tapping attempts — security and geolocation assurance products rather than computing ones.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Fiber-tap detection and location attestation are buyable today by telcos, exchanges and defense — the first quantum networking revenue is likely to be security, not entanglement-enabled computing.
insights.quote: Quantum Alarm to monitor network security by detecting fiber tapping attempts
insights.locator: This could include Quantum Position Verification (QPV)
